item.title: DeepSeek Harness: Interesting Architecture, but Is It the Right Choice for Building Agents?
item.description:
DeepSeek Harness: Interesting Architecture, but Is It the Right Choice for Building Agents?

A staff-engineering perspective on DeepSeek Harness — what the plugin architecture actually buys you, where it adds integration cost, and which teams it is genuinely built for.

[!NOTE]

Executive TL;DR

DeepSeek Harness (open-sourced August 13, 2026, MIT) is a modular agent runtime built on the Cordis plugin framework. Its formula: Agent = Model + Harness, where every major capability — model, tools, session, sandbox, even the agent loop itself — is a replaceable plugin.

item.title: The Self-Declaration Principle: Why Handoffs Only Works When Agents Know Their Own Edges
item.description:
The Self-Declaration Principle: Why Handoffs Only Works When Agents Know Their Own Edges

After reading the LangChain taxonomy post and writing my own breakdown of the call-by-call numbers, I still had a nagging feeling I didn’t fully understand Handoffs. Not the mechanics — the handoff tool is simple enough. What I didn’t understand was why Handoffs produces the call-count advantages it claims, and under what conditions it actually behaves like the pattern the diagrams promise.
